Every rule listed under `spec_rules` is expected to exist in the DB seed with the
same fix_type and applies_to. The `known_deviations` block whitelists specific
documented drifts so they don't fail CI while the analyst rules on them.
Also see docs/spec-conformance-audit.md — the human-readable matrix behind this file.
Every entry here corresponds to a row in docs/spec-conformance-audit.md.
Removing a deviation entry re-arms the gate against that specific drift.
Adding a new entry requires updating the audit doc — the two files are locked together.
